subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should OpenClaw silently skip `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files larger than 4 MiB during workspace scans as the default OOM mitigation after the symlink-chain regression is repaired?
rationale: The byte cap is a narrow availability fix, but silently dropping ignore rules changes scan semantics for existing over-cap files and should be an explicit maintainer policy choice.

options.title: Accept Bounded Skip After Repair
options.body: Keep the 4 MiB cap after preserving symlink chains and getting real workspace-scan proof, accepting that over-cap ignore files are not applied.

options.title: Require Visible Diagnostic
options.body: Ask for a warning or diagnostic so users can tell when ignore rules were skipped because a file exceeded the cap.

options.title: Choose A Different Read Policy
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want streaming, a different threshold, partial handling, or configurable behavior instead of silent skip.

recommendation.title: Accept Bounded Skip After Repair
recommendation.body: Keep the 4 MiB cap after preserving symlink chains and getting real workspace-scan proof, accepting that over-cap ignore files are not applied.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the shared ignore-rule helper and central caller wiring that owns this scan-policy boundary.
